title: Hives (urticaria) visit
what: Hives are itchy welts on the skin, like a nettle sting. The patches appear and fade quickly. The doctor looks for the cause and chooses the treatment.
why: When itchy welts appear on the skin, once or repeatedly over weeks.
duration: the visit usually takes 20 to 30 minutes; tests as the doctor orders
tell_doctor: When it started, how long patches last and how often they come
What you ate, what medicines you took, and what happened before the rash
Whether your lips, eyelids or tongue swelled
All medicines and supplements you take

prepare.title: Photos
prepare.text: Take photos of the rash. It may be gone by the visit.

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: Write down when the rash appeared and what came before it.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your own medicines. If you take an allergy medicine, tell the doctor.

bring: A list of medicines and supplements
steps: The doctor asks about the rash in detail
Sometimes draws a finger across the skin to check the reaction
Chooses a medicine and explains how to take it
feel: Itching can be severe. Treatment usually helps quickly
after: Take the medicine as the doctor said, even if the rash has gone
Avoid whatever triggers the rash, if known
Do not wear tight clothes or take hot baths during a flare-up
If the rash lasts more than 6 weeks, come back for another visit
red_flags: Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, trouble swallowing or breathing: call your local emergency number
Weakness, dizziness or fainting together with the rash: call your local emergency number

faq.a: No. They do not pass from person to person.

faq.q: Is it always a food allergy?
faq.a: No. Often the cause cannot be found. It can follow infections or medicines. The doctor will help work it out.

reminders.text: Visit about hives tomorrow. Bring photos of the rash and your list of medicines.
